recognize_zh: Wright 染色骨髓抹片中多顆未增大的紅血球含細小環狀滋養體（黑箭頭）、線狀裂殖子（白箭頭）與疑似分裂中的形態（紅箭頭），無色素、無配子體，符合紅血球內巴貝西蟲（Babesia）。
features: Many red cells contain small intraerythrocytic parasites; infected cells are not enlarged
Delicate ring-form trophozoites with a small chromatin dot (black arrow)
Paired or budding forms suggestive of binary fission (red arrow)
No hemozoin pigment, no Schüffner stippling, no gametocytes or schizonts
Some small extracellular dot-like forms in background
describe_en: Wright-stained bone marrow aspirate smear shows numerous red cells containing small intraerythrocytic parasites without red cell enlargement. Multiple forms are present, including delicate ring-like trophozoites (black arrow), elongated linear merozoites (white arrow), and paired/budding forms suggestive of division (red arrow). There is no hemozoin pigment, no stippling, and no gametocytes or schizonts. Findings are consistent with Babesia infection; parasitemia should be quantified on the peripheral blood smear and confirmed with PCR.

ddx.vs: P. falciparum rings are uniform with frequent accolé forms and may show crescent gametocytes and pigment, whereas Babesia shows pleomorphic rings, linear and dividing forms, and extracellular parasites without pigment.
These inclusions are solid dots without a ring of cytoplasm and do not show paired or tetrad arrangements.
Overlying platelets are granular with a halo and lie in a different focal plane rather than forming discrete rings within the red cell.
Precipitate is distributed across the slide including between cells and lacks the uniform ring and chromatin structure of parasites.
